Commentary.Commentary: The quickies, Cummins and Holder held the lines properly and didn't allow India any freebies. Miguel Cummins was the real cracker as he took 6 wickets as the Indians looked to score freely and threw their wickets eventually. Talking about the target of 346, is it achievable in minimum 87 overs? Will Windies go for a draw or a win? Or the hosts will show the zeal to win it as they have an upper hand. Do join us in a bit for the same.

The Indian team have finally declared after scoring 60-plus runs in this 9-over span. Rahane and Rohit wanted to get to a flier but unfortunately Rohit was given out in a harsh decision. The next batsman Saha was also given out off a no ball. Towards the end, Jadeja smashed quick runs and made India cross 340-plus runs.

The players are out in the middle. AJINKYA RAHANE has just crossed his half-century and ROHIT SHARMA is not far behind. MIGUEL CUMMINS will open the bowling proceedings. How will both sides fare in the morning session?

India had the upper hand at that point with a lead of 128 but they picked up where they left off with the bat. KL Rahul and Shikhar Dhawan got them off to a good start and Ajinkya Rahane and Rohit Sharma cemented it. Miguel Cummins and Roston Chase impressed with the ball yesterday and will hope to do the same today while the visitors will mostly declare early, setting a target around the 300-run mark. It seems like we might have a conclusive end to this game. Stay tuned for the ball-by-ball commentary as we take you through today's action.

Hello and a warm welcome to the final day of the 3rd Test between West Indies and India. The Indians made a statement with their commanding show yesterday. Bhuvneshwar Kumar stole the show with the ball, cutting West Indies' innings short with a fifer. Jermaine Blackwood and Marlon Samuels tried their best but were only able to put up a 67-run stand.
... Day 5, Session 1 ...

The visitors already have a substantial 285-run lead and they won't hesitate in piling on the runs tomorrow before an early declaration. West Indies will surely go after those wickets to slow down and leave the batsmen shaken. It's going to be a gritty final day but both sides have enormous heart. Join us at 1900 IST for the final day of the Test. Until then... Cheers and take care!

Despite the late day heroics of Rahane and Sharma, the day undoubtedly belonged to Bhuvneshwar Kumar. His efforts today almost single-handedly dismantled the Windies batting line-up. His fifer came at crucial moments, never allowing the home side to settle down and eat into the lead. Jermaine Blackwood and Marlon Samuels did their best, with a 67-run partnership, but that was the highlight of their innings.

This time it was Miguel Cummins who drew first blood for the hosts, and he was quick to follow it up with the big wicket of Virat Kohli. The golden-armed Roston Chase also started off strong, taking out the stubborn Dhawan. Brathwaite was decent as well but there was not a lot the bowlers could do to hold back the batsmen towards the end.

Curtains on Day 4 and the visitors will be mightily pleased with the results. They impressed with both bat and ball, carrying their momentum into the final session with a lightening 85-run partnership between Ajinkya Rahane and Rohit Sharma. The Indian batting line-up, shaken by the loss of Kohli and Dhawan, was shored up by the Rahane-Sharma duo, with their booming shots to end the day on a high note.
